sections.h2: Which selling routes make sense in Tinley Park?
sections.html:
A Tinley Park owner can list with a broker, market the house alone, or sell as-is to a buyer paying cash. The village straddles two counties, so the first job is to see which one your parcel belongs to.

Tinley Park is a southern suburb of Chicago covering about 16.2 square miles, with Cook County townships Bremen, Orland and Rich and Will County's Frankfort Township under one village government. The Census Bureau counted 56,703 residents in 2010 and 55,971 in 2020, and estimates 55,140 for July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: Does Cook County or Will County handle my Tinley Park house?
sections.html:
The county that holds your parcel number sends the tax bill, hears assessment appeals and records the deed, whatever the village line says. Part of the village lies in Will County, and that side includes the Brookside Marketplace shopping center.

The two counties run separate offices. Look at the latest tax bill, spot the county, and ask that county's treasurer where the account stands. Cook County's due dates change from year to year, as the table further down shows.

The village's four townships are Bremen, Orland and Rich on the Cook side and Frankfort on the Will side. The township matters when you look up an assessment or a past appeal, so note it from the parcel record before you call either county.

sections.h2: What do Tinley Park homes and households look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's five-year survey results sketch a village of long-term owners, many of whom drive a long way to work.

  • Households that own: 86.9% of occupied homes
  • Middle value among owned homes: $299,900
  • Middle monthly rent, utilities included: $1,495
  • 22,320 households, about 2.45 people each
  • Household income at the midpoint: $105,189
  • Stayed put over the prior twelve months: 92.0%
  • Travel to work: 33.7 minutes on average
  • Share in the 65-and-over group: 21.5%

sections.h2: Where does Tinley Park sit, and what is its housing stock?
sections.html:
The village borders Oak Forest to the northeast, Orland Park to the northwest, Orland Hills and Mokena to the west, Country Club Hills to the east, Matteson to the southeast and Frankfort to the southwest. Village government uses a council-manager structure.

Counting day in 2020 turned up 22,751 housing units, and 3.3% sat vacant. Within that, 1.1% of owner homes and 7.5% of rentals were empty. Residents had a median age of 43.0. Later survey work puts adult bachelor's attainment at 37.0% and the foreign-born share at 9.3%.

Shopping carries a lot of weight here: 2022 Census figures show about $1.81 billion in retail sales, roughly $33,380 for every resident, while health care and social services took in about $361 million.

Settlers arrived in the 1820s, and by the 1840s a large German community had formed, so the village took the name Bremen when it was founded in 1853. It was renamed Tinley Park in 1890 for the first station agent at the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific depot and incorporated on June 27, 1892.

The railroad drew a washing machine factory in 1905 and a cola bottling plant that ran into the 1950s. The big change came later: between 1970 and 1994, more than 11,000 housing units were built, mostly west and south of the original center. The village has since worked on its historic downtown, which follows the 1892 boundaries, and the outdoor amphitheater that opened in 1990 now holds about 28,000 people per event.

sections.h2: Which schools and commuter routes serve Tinley Park?
sections.html:
Four elementary districts cover the village: Kirby District 140, Community Consolidated District 146, Summit Hill District 161 and Elementary District 159. Victor J. Andrew High School in District 230 and Tinley Park High School in Bremen District 228 are both in the village, while small areas feed Lincoln-Way East and Rich Central. Residents are mostly in the Moraine Valley Community College district, with the rest in South Suburban College or Joliet Junior College territory.

Metra's Rock Island District has two stations here, Tinley Park on Oak Park Avenue and the 80th Avenue station. Pace runs routes 356, 364 and 386. The main roads are I-80 east to west, Harlem Avenue (IL 43) north to south, 159th Street (US 6) in the north and La Grange Road (US 45) at the western edge.

sections.h2: Which dates does Cook County use for Tinley Park tax installments?
sections.html:
Cook County's due dates move. The Treasurer's Office due dates page lists these recent ones.

Cook County property tax installment due dates, tax years 2023 to 2025
Tax yearFirst installmentSecond installment
2023March 1, 2024August 1, 2024
2024March 4, 2025December 15, 2025
2025April 1, 2026October 1, 2026

The Treasurer also lists exemptions that Cook owners can apply for, including the homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, disability, home improvement, military, disabled veteran and first responder's surviving spouse programs. On the Will County side, the Treasurer explains that delinquent taxes become a lien that tax buyers purchase at an annual sale, and homeowners typically have one to three years to redeem before a buyer can start court action.

sections.h2: What does the Tinley Park Building Division require?
sections.html:
Most home improvements and additions call for building, electrical or plumbing permits, and the Building Division asks owners to call 708-444-5100 before starting if they are unsure. A homeowner may do work on their own property, with the exception that changing electric service needs a licensed electrical contractor. Any contractor the owner hires must be licensed and bonded with the village before work starts.

  • Apply with one copy of your plat of survey, normally provided at your closing, and any drawings or sketches.
  • Post the building permit placard at the site until the work is complete.
  • Starting without a permit can bring a fine.
  • The village's plan-review consultant does inspections on weekday mornings until noon.

The village notes that its comprehensive building code was revised and adopted on July 20, 2026, and lists the 2024 International codes among the current ones.

sections.h2: What if the Tinley Park mortgage is in default?
sections.html:
The Building Division page points to a Foreclosure Property Registration Program run through ProChamps, with a separate page for defaulted mortgage property registration. If a lender has started foreclosure on your home, ask the Building Division whether registration applies to you.

State law treats a few of these transfers differently. Under 765 ILCS 77/15, a borrower who hands the lender a deed in place of foreclosure, or who agrees to a consent judgment, is excused from the seller disclosure report. A regular sale still needs the report in the buyer's hands ahead of signing, as 765 ILCS 77/20 requires.

Investors who buy Tinley Park commercial space use a separate Change of Use/Owner application with a $50 fee, which does not apply to homes.

faqs.q: Which county does a Tinley Park address belong to?
faqs.a: Either one. The village covers parts of Cook and Will counties, and the county named on your bill decides which treasurer and which recording office you deal with.

faqs.q: What are the tax installment dates for a Tinley Park house in Cook County?
faqs.a: They shift from year to year. The first installment fell on March 4 in 2025 and on April 1 in 2026, with the second on December 15, 2025 and October 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Does a Tinley Park basement remodel need village sign-off?
faqs.a: Most improvements and additions need a permit of some kind. Ring 708-444-5100 for the Building Division to confirm your project, and bring the plat of survey from your closing.

faqs.q: What if a Tinley Park owner gives the lender a deed in lieu?
faqs.a: The state exempts that kind of transfer from the seller disclosure report, though the deed itself still gets recorded at the county.

faqs.q: How quickly can a cash buyer close on a Tinley Park house?
faqs.a: Title work, payoff letters and the agreed closing date set the pace. Without a mortgage there is no underwriting to wait on, and the county records the deed afterward.
